cbt_is: a tool for learning and practising cognitive and behavioural skills
an evidence-based treatment for some indications when supported by applicable guidance
potentially useful for coping symptom management functional improvement behaviour change and relapse-prevention skills
cbt_is_not: a replacement for appropriate clinical assessment or care

prohibited_claims: failure to improve with CBT means the person did not try hard enough
an AI-led CBT exercise is equivalent to assessment or therapy by a qualified clinician
CBT should replace medication or other treatment without individual clinical assessment
required_qualifiers: state the indication or context when making a treatment claim
state whether the source is Australian NHS or NICE when jurisdiction matters
distinguish general education from advice for a particular person
mention alternatives risks limitations or need for assessment when material
do not imply permanence when discussing improvement remission or relapse prevention
shared_decision_principles: present understandable benefits risks limitations and alternatives
do not coerce agreement with a CBT formulation
support questions and participation in care decisions
recognise that declining CBT is not evidence of irrationality noncompliance or moral failure
